claims.text: As-cast equimolar CoCrFeNiTi is a single-phase, homogeneous, disordered solid solution.
The as-cast equimolar CoCrFeNiTi alloy has relatively low hardness.
The as-cast equimolar CoCrFeNiTi alloy has relatively low strength.
The as-cast equimolar CoCrFeNiTi alloy has good plasticity and machinability.
A homogeneous disordered solid solution limits the development of nanoscale compositionally ordered precipitates in equimolar CoCrFeNiTi.
Nanoscale compositionally ordered precipitates would act as effective obstacles to dislocation motion.
The absence of nanoscale ordered obstacles causes the relatively low hardness and yield strength of the as-cast alloy.
The absence of nanoscale ordered obstacles permits the alloy to retain favorable plasticity and machinability.
Annealing at an intermediate temperature can induce short-range chemical ordering or early-stage precipitation in CoCrFeNiTi.
The annealing treatment will produce coherent nanoscale ordered regions or precipitates in the matrix.
Annealing-induced ordered regions or precipitates increase the density of obstacles to dislocation glide.
The nanoscale barriers increase lattice friction and resistance to plastic deformation.
The annealed alloy will have significantly higher hardness than the as-cast alloy.
The annealed alloy will have significantly higher compressive strength than the as-cast alloy.
The annealed alloy will have lower plastic strain than the as-cast alloy while retaining some ductility.
